title: Levels-of-Analysis Lab (Ecological Fallacy)
description: Paste a group-level table (group label, n, mean X, mean Y) and get the n-weighted ecological (group-level) correlation, computed closed-form across group means. Compare it against a known or assumed individual-level correlation you supply, and the tool flags a levels-of-analysis reversal or magnitude-inflation risk when the two disagree. Two built-in worked examples ship: Robinson's 1950 published state-vs-individual literacy/foreign-born reversal (textbook figures, informational) and a synthetic school-level income-vs-test-score illustration (editable group table).
data_vintage: Robinson example reproduces published 1950 textbook correlation figures (static, never refreshed, informational only — no raw microdata). School-income example is a synthetic illustrative dataset, not real school data. Primary use is a user-pasted group table; the tool holds no live or refreshable data.
regulatory_citations: Robinson, W.S. (1950). "Ecological Correlations and the Behavior of Individuals." American Sociological Review 15(3):351-357.

mcp_tool_definition.name: levels_of_analysis_lab
mcp_tool_definition.description: Compute the n-weighted ecological (group-level) correlation from a user-supplied table of group means, compare it against a user-supplied individual-level correlation, and flag a levels-of-analysis reversal or magnitude-inflation risk (ecological fallacy) when the two disagree.
